title: Financial Aid — Gunnison County Health and Human Services — 220 N Spruce St - Gunnison County
summary: Financial Aid includes:  The Old Age Pension (OAP) program. - Basic financial and health care assistance for people who are 60 years or older. - To apply for the Old Age Pension program you must be a Colorado resident and you must apply in the county where you live. Colorado Works/Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF)  - A federal program that provides cash assistance to eligible low-income pregnant women and single and two-parent families with dependent children    while working to secure or improve employment and achieve self-sufficiency. -  Colorado Works/TANF clients may also apply for Food Assistance/SNAP and Health First Colorado (Colorado's Medicaid Program). -  Cooperation with Child Support Services is required unless good cause is established. - Child Care Assistance and other supportive services may be available for those prepared for or seeking employment. If approved for Colorado Works/TANF, recipients may be required to participate in a work related activity. - Undocumented immigrants are not eligible to receive Colorado Works/TANF, but US born citizen children of undocumented immigrants may be    eligible for Colorado Works/TANF if the family meets all other eligibility criteria. - A minor parent, you must attend high school or a GED program and live with your parents or in another approved setting. Aid to the Blind & Aid to the Needy Disabled       - Provides a small cash assistance benefit to low-income Colorado residents age 18 - 59 who have at least a six-month total disability that precludes    them from working. - Must be  low-income and meet the Social Security Administration's definition of blindness. - Other income such as wages or Veteran's Assistance, may reduce the amount of the AND/AB payment. - There are no medical benefits provided by the AND/AB program. - Client applying for AND will have Medicaid and will need to see their Primary Care Physicians to complete AND exam requirements. If clients do not    have a doctor they can go to www.colorado.gov/pacific/hcpf/find-doctor . When the primary diagnosis is alcoholism or drug abuse, the AND recipient:      - Is limited to 12 cumulative months in a lifetime;     - Must agree to and participate in treatment;     - Must submit to random testing; and     - Will lose AND benefits if he/she tests positive for alcohol or drugs two times in any three-month period.

fields.organization name: Habitat for Humanity of Pueblo Inc
fields.detailed services: Ramp Construction Services; Landscaping Services; Home Rehabilitation Services
fields.service summary: Minor Repair Program that will include exterior work such as painting, patching, minor repair and landscaping. Tasks may include repair of siding, trim, exterior needs related to handicap accessibility,  paint and tree trimming.
fields.eligibility: Demonstrate Need - Applicants must lack adequate resources or ability to accomplish minor exterior repairs and maintenance, landscaping, clean-up, or painting on their own. Applicants must be seeking repairs for a home that they own and occupy. Have an Ability to Pay - Applicants must demonstrate that their household income is less than the maximum allowable income. Household income will include the income of all adults living in the home who are 18 years-old or older. Willingness to Partner - Applicants are required to turn in complete applications. Each applicant is required to be present and engaged on their construction site while Habitat staff and volunteers are working. This means that all members of the household who are over the age of 18 will be willing to provide ten hours of volunteer time, or sweat equity, to assist with the repair project. Area Served: Pueblo County
fields.access method: How to Apply: Forms available online or in person
fields.required documents: Applicant must be a legal resident of the U.S. The property must be located in Pueblo County. The home must have been constructed after 1977 to eliminate asbestos and lead abatement concerns. The property must not be in danger of foreclosure and mortgage payments must be current. Applicant must be able to provide certificate of current homeowner's insurance. The home, property, and the surrounding area must be deemed a safe working environment for the project and volunteers. Habitat will perform a background check on each applicant, individuals who have been convicted of crimes against children or sexually violent offenses will not be eligible to participate.
